en: Urgh, god <Italic>damn</Italic>!
Listen.
I used to be yakuza, just like you. So I get that you're trying to protect your boss.
But I want what's best for this town. Same as you.
And the only way I can keep this town safe is by talking to Yahata and stopping the Tojo Clan.
So please. Tell me where he is.
The hideout's crawlin' with men, all there to guard the boss.
Y'set foot in there, yer as good as dead.
Just tell me where it is, and I'll handle it. Even if I have to knock sense into every last one of them.
That so? Hahaha! Ain't many in Nagasu with those kinda balls.
Fine then. It's all on you.
You'll find the boss's hideout <Color:7>around the middle of Suzukake Lane<Color:Default>.
And hey... Good luck. All o' Nagasugai's countin' on ya.
I won't let you down.
What the shit? You're the asshole who came stormin' through our HQ yesterday.
That's right. Now tell me where I can find Yahata. We need to talk.
Heh, I knew you'd say that. I hear y'been snoopin' around town lookin' for him.
That's right. So? Where is he?
It's my turn for questions first. Why d'ya gotta see him so bad?
I made a promise to Madarame.
I told him I wouldn't let Aoyama and the Tojo Clan have the run of the place. That I'd protect Nagasugai and the Yamagasa Family.
Y'sayin' <Italic>you</Italic> talked to the patriarch?
I did.
Hmph. N' why should I believe ya?
You'll understand once I see Yahata.
Sorry, but the boss got real hurt yesterday.
Can't just let ya waltz into our hideout. Guy like ya could be workin' for the Tojo Clan fer all I know.
A hideout, huh?
So that's where I'll find Yahata.
Not if I can help it! You ain't leavin' here alive!
So this is where Yahata's camping out.
Who the hell're you?
Doesn't matter. I heard I could find Yahata here.
What? The captain's⑬ Er, I mean, I never heard that name before!
Sounds like I've got the right place. Guess I'll just show myself in.
Hey! You can't go in there!
We got trouble. Yeah. Guy in a trenchcoat.
Oh, hey, Saejima-san. Aren't you supposed to be in the infirmary?
Yeah, you're not scheduled for a shift today. Besides, you just got smacked around by those shady woodworkers.
Not a good time to be wandering around, you know?
I'm fine. Got any idea where Baba-chan's gone?
Wait, did you come out here because you're worried they'll go after him?
It crossed my mind.
You're thinking about Baba's parole bid, aren't you?
Well, there's nothing to worry about on that front. After you went into the infirmary, Baba went to Deputy Warden. He's probably in his hearing right now.
Oh, wow. Really?
It's all finally happening for Baba.
He's been determined to get his parole and live a normal life.
Well hey, that's great, then!
He sure seemed to be agonizing over it. Heck, I wasn't so sure he'd get out, even if he is a good kid.
He once said to me, "They call it 'paying your debt to society', but sitting in here and doing nothing doesn't pay back shit."
"That's why I have to get out of here and do things that truly atone for my sins."
He had morality, but he was scared of acting on it. You gave him the courage to act, Saejima.
Huh? There's Deputy Warden. Did he already finish with Baba-chan's hearing?
Uh... I don't see Baba...
Hang on, I'll go ask a guard.
What's the word?
Um... Apparently Baba's hearing ended over an hour ago.
Where is he, then?
Weird seeing you out here, boss. You usually spend rec time cooped up alone in our cell. Something wrong?
Hey, I come out sometimes.
N' quit it with that boss crap. I already told ya I don't like it.
What's the big deal? I'm just being respectful!
Only appropriate for Saejima-san, the great tiger of the Tojo Clan.
Who told ya that?
No one in particular. It's just floating around the place.
They say you're a legendary murderer who once took out eighteen guys in a single hit.
I mean, you had to have known people'd catch wind of your life outside.
Oh, right. Speaking of the outside, isn't it almost time?
Time for what?
Your parole, boss! Duh.
You've been here what, two years now?
Somethin' like that.
And you got sentenced to three years for assault, right?
That means you could be out of here in no time if they approve your parole.
Too bad that's a damn big if.
You got that. The deputy warden here is a real cold customer.
Yup. As harsh as they come.
We'll be just fine as long as we stay out of his way. Don't stand out; that's the quickest way to <Italic>get</Italic> out.
By the way, Baba-chan was looking for you, boss.
Baba?
ctx: diálogo uid0002071e + frase de acompañante/calle STID_ST_K_GESUI01

en: Oh c'mon. Don't tell me you forgot who he is.
The one shacking up in our cell!
Oh, the kid.
Pretty sure Baba-chan's looking for advice or something. Not sure what on.
I offered to lend him an ear, but he said it needed to be someone in his own line of work.
His line of work? So he's yakuza, too...
Anyway, I dunno what's eating him, but you should probably go impart some of your sagely criminal wisdom.
N' where's he at now?
Not sure. Oh, but Oshima-san would probably know.
I mean, all he ever does during rec time is sit his ass down on that bench.
Alright, I'll see if he knows anythin'.
What can I do for you, Saejima-san? Do you need some more painkillers?
Naw, just came for a bit o' exercise.
If you say so. By the way, it's been months now since that gang started coming for you, but you haven't said a peep to anyone else in the cell.
'Course I haven't. Can't go gettin' them involved.
I wonder, though. Why are those thugs so pissed off at you?
Is it for something you did on the outside?
Doubt it. I was only out for a year. Can't do much to offend in that time.
You say that, but they've been zeroed in on you ever since they got here. And that was almost six months ago now...
You really think there's no reason for that?
Maybe they got a bone to pick with the organization I was workin' for.
Maybe. Either way, be careful. I thought they were your typical prison gang... but this is something completely different.
You might need a lot more than just painkillers if things go south next time.
...I've been wondering. Why don't you fight back?
Can't. I got my reasons.
I gotta get out. Whatever happens, no matter what they do, I gotta keep persistin'.
Freedom, huh. So that's why you don't retaliate.
Still, you won't survive in here if you keep letting them beat you like that. Have you talked to the guards?
Why not? I'm sure Deputy Warden Kosaka would listen.
A strict man like him would never tolerate such flagrant rulebreaking. Worth a try, right?
Dunno if I can trust him. Dunno if I can trust anyone.
Because of Penitentiary No. 2? I've heard the rumors. It didn't sound pleasant, to say the least.
But this is a legitimate prison. You should give reporting those maniacs some serious thought.
Oh, and the kid's been looking for you. The one from our cell?
Yeah, Baba-chan. Himura mentioned the same thing.
Poor kid. He's worried he won't get out.
On parole?
Mhm. I'm not sure why he's so eager, either. It's not like anyone's ever visited him here.
I asked him why once, and he broke down in tears.
Really? Baba cried?
Well. That's when I learned he killed a man for his family, and then his family abandoned him. Who wouldn't weep?
He's in for murder!?
I know. I was shocked, too. He seems so timid. Must've been scared shitless when he did it.
And then his family ditched him. I suppose that's normal in the yakuza world, but still.
Murder... So he must've served a lot of time before he even got here.
Oh yeah. He's been in prison for ten years. Did the kill when he was twenty.
Now he's going to re-enter society after being gone a decade. And with no home, no family...
(Poor kid.)
He's gonna have to deal with all that soon. Just a few more days before his parole gets approved.
Hm... I had no idea.
Yeah. Look, you're from the same dark underbelly of society as he is, right?
So talk to him, will ya? We're cellmates, after all.
Hey, ya know Baba? From our cell?
Uh-huh... Saw him earlier.
Really? Ya see where he went?
Mm... You know that creep Kugihara and his gang?
Baba went off with them to the storeroom. That was hours ago, though.
He went with those guys!?
Bad news. Baba⑬
Yeah. I just heard.
Those bastards. It wasn't enough to go after you; they had to target the kid as well?
We gotta get to the storeroom!
Hey, the kid that shanked that guy earlier... isn't he your cellmate?
Hard to believe such a nice-looking fella would do that.
Well, do ya actually know anythin' about him?
Nope. Can't say I do. I've hardly talked to the guy.
That's what I thought.
I did see the guards hauling him off to solitary, though.
Interestin'...
Say, d'ya know Baba?
Yeah, I'm with him on the maintenance crew.
Good. Say, you guys use chisels in your work?
Chisel? The wood-carving tool?
Not really... They call us maintenance, but all we actually do is shovel snow.
I mean, I can't say for sure that we never use them, but I've never needed to myself.
Hm... okay.
(Gotta find someone with better info.)
Ya got a minute?
Who's in the know here? Who knows what's goin' on?
Uh, that would be him.
That old-timer?
Yup. He's a pretty old hand here. He's got connections with the guards, I hear.
He's pretty much Abashiri's power broker. Definitely has a lot of control over the flow of goods and information.
Gotcha. Ya been a great help.
Nice job. It's been a while since I laughed so hard! Fun doesn't come around here much.
Did ya get what I asked for?
Uh-huh. Number 134. That's the number on Kugihara's chisel.
Okay. Now, if we can just get the chisel itself...
And that'll prove Baba's innocence, huh?
I see. Hey, here's a little bonus for you. Kind of like when a bank gives you a toaster for opening an account.
You got an <Color:8>Ointment<Color:Default>.
Thanks. And by the way, banks don't really do that anymore.
Ah. Well, I guess I don't know the modern ways of thanking your customers...
What can I do for you now?
The chisels all got numbers, and they're assigned to certain woodworkers, who are the only guys allowed to take 'em out. Kugihara's a woodworker. Ain't all that correct?
Yeah. So?
I want to know Kugihara's chisel number.
Hah, you think he's guilty, right off the bat. Ever occur to you that Baba might actually be the culprit, just as it looks?
Never mind that. Can ya do it?
Of course. So, here's what you can do for me.
Another delivery job?
Nope. See the guard there?
I need you to catch his attention and keep it a while. How about you... make him chase you?
Be a decoy, ya mean?
Yeah. You catch on fast.
Here, take this with you.
'Kay...
You got <Color:8>Mystery Envelope<Color:Default>.
It's finished.
So it is.
Well? Any news?
Sure. You wish to know about inmates with access to chisels, yes? That would be the woodworking and leathercraft crews. Them, and only them.
Leathercraft?
Yeah. They make goods like wallets and purses, then sell them to distributors.
Okay, just those two crews. Ya sure?
Haha. Doubt me if you want. But I know a lot more...
For instance, it's been a long time since any orders for leather came in. Weak economy, doncha know...
In fact, the last two years, there's been no leathercrafting at all. You'll find neither hide nor hair of it... hehehe!
...Wow.
Anyway, that means the only convicts with chisel access are the woodworkers. That's a fact.
Another fact: every chisel is marked with a unique number.
Inmates can only use the chisel that's assigned to them.
Makes sense. Woulda been pretty dumb if the guards weren't keepin' track of such obvious shanks.
One last fact⑬you'll like this one. One of the woodworkers is... Kugihara.
Huh! Now that's interestin'. Thanks, old-timer.
(So the chisel's from the woodworking crew for sure, but we don't know who it belongs to.)
(I should get back to Himura.)
Didn't figure you to be the info man.
Kind of a rude way to introduce yourself there. Just because we're in prison doesn't mean you shouldn't use your etiquette, Taiga Saejima-san.
Guess I shouldn't be surprised you know my name.
Please. I'm the info man. Of course, a celebrity like you, everyone inside knows who you are.
So. You want to know things that'll help you clear Shigeki Baba of assault. That's mighty big of you, trying to help the kid.
I can see ya already know a lot about it. Well then, let's skip ahead to where ya tell me the source of the damn chisel.
Haha, you make it sound easy. But they're being tight-lipped and even tighter-assed about this one. It's bad, bad mojo, believe me.
